questions: Should the color bar represent the KDE density values (as in the reference solution) or the distribution of the samples themselves (e.g., mapping sample values to colors)?
Is the color bar required to be explicitly labeled (e.g., 'Density') or is an unlabeled color bar acceptable?
Should the KDE plot use a specific color palette or colormap, or is any default acceptable?
Does 'indicating the mean and standard deviation' require explicit markers, lines, or text annotations on the plot, or is it sufficient that they are parameters of the distribution?
Should the plot include a title or axis labels (e.g., 'Normal Distribution', 'Value', 'Density')?
Is the random seed applied only to sample generation, or should it also affect any other random elements (e.g., KDE bandwidth estimation if stochastic)?
Should the function create a new figure for each call, or is it acceptable to plot on the current axes if one exists?
What should be the exact return value: the Axes object from the KDE plot (as in reference) or the color bar's Axes, or something else?
